title: MOFA welcomes Japan-Germany joint leaders’ statement reaffirming importance of peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait
text:
Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung welcomes and expresses appreciation for the joint statement issued following a summit meeting between Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Tokyo on October 28. In the joint statement, the two leaders emphasized the importance of maintaining peace and security across the Taiwan Strait and called for the peaceful resolution of cross-strait issues.

During a joint press conference, Prime Minister Takaichi reiterated that security and prosperity in the Euro-Atlantic and the Indo-Pacific areas were increasingly intertwined. Chancellor Merz noted that the principle prohibiting the use of force enshrined in the UN Charter applied equally to the Taiwan Strait, and urged relevant countries and regions to act with prudence.

The joint statement also expressed serious concern over the situation in the East China Sea and the South China Sea, reiterating strong opposition to any unilateral attempts to change the status quo by force or coercion anywhere in the world. Furthermore, the two leaders voiced grave concern over the increasing use of economic coercion, such as the arbitrary export restrictions on critical minerals, and rejected nonmarket policies and practices that were leading to overcapacity and market distortions.

They also reaffirmed that Japan and Germany were “premium partners” and decided on the early convening of the next bilateral 2+2 consultations between their foreign affairs and defense ministries. To enhance supply chain resilience, they pledged to foster cooperation in a wide range of areas, including semiconductors, critical raw materials, AI, energy, and such defense-related industries as uncrewed systems.

The Japanese and German leaders’ expression of serious concern over the Taiwan Strait underscores the fact that maintaining peace and stability in the area has become a consensus among and a common interest of the international community.

Peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait serve as an indispensable cornerstone for regional security and the prosperity of the international community, as they are inextricably linked to global economic security and supply chains.

Guided by the principles of integrated diplomacy, Taiwan will continue to deepen exchanges and collaboration with Japan, Germany, and other like-minded nations to uphold freedom, democracy, and the rules-based international order and jointly promote peace, stability, and prosperity throughout the region. (E)
